b:
My father has three sisters. Since she was the eldest, I called her Periya Mami. In the beginning she was one of the people I was afraid of.. I remember being frightened to see her wrapped up against the Margazhi mist, picking flowers at the house in Kandarodai.. Where that fear went later, I don't know..

After we came to Wellawatte, Mami lived downstairs and we upstairs.. From then on there was one kitchen for both houses.. When it came to cooking snacks, no one could compete with Mami.. not even my mother.. Because I liked her vadai, she would set aside a separate plate just for me. To this day no one has matched Mami's vadai for me

The elder of our house was our Periyappa.. After him, that place belonged to Mami.

Tamil, religion, astrology, general knowledge, cooking, drama: you could rely on her for all of it.. She would keep even a newspaper snippet she had read somewhere, some time. Of everyone in our house she had the strongest reading habit. Whenever she found time she would read something

When we couldn't find an answer in the Virakesari crossword, it was her we went to. She would surely teach us something new.

She had been on pilgrimage to Kashi. Her faith in God was intense. She began each day by sprinkling water and putting on holy ash. She knew everything there was to know about temples..

Though she came through many trials and sorrows, old age chased her down and caught her.

Old age brought illness

Finally, one phone call. When she said, "It's unbearable, come and do something for me, da," I fell silent, helpless. That day she also taught me the horror of that word

Now she has fallen silent for ever. Those hands will not cook again. Those eyes will not look for books again. The dry frond has fallen from our palm tree. The great elder of our family has left us. What will we do now?
note: Periya Mami: the eldest aunt. Margazhi is the cold, misty Tamil month of December–January; Kandarodai is a village near Jaffna. The Virakesari is a Tamil daily newspaper in Sri Lanka. The title recalls the saying "when the dry palm frond falls, the tender frond laughs", about the old giving way to the young.
